Sources: nuxt.com releases/blog v4-4 and v4-6 notes, vuejs/router v5.0.0 notes. The only nit is that Nuxt 4.4's createUseFetch factory could replace the hand-rolled wrapper in usePageData.ts:5.

The empty devDependencies means no lint/typecheck tooling of the app's own (see churn finding), but that doesn't add weight.

churn_resistance.rationale: The architecture ages well: PokeAPI knowledge is behind one module, pages go through one composable, and there is no reliance on framework internals, so a Nuxt 5 (Nitro v3/h3 v2) upgrade would touch almost nothing. What costs it is duplication the framework already offers a cure for — humanize twice, the excluded-type list twice, and response shapes redeclared in five pages instead of shared/types — none of which the build ever type-checks.

findings.issue: The 18-type business rule ('stellar', 'unknown', 'shadow' excluded) is duplicated inline although server/utils/pokeapi.ts:75 already defines EXCLUDED_TYPES; the two can drift.
findings.suggestion: Export a isPlayableType(name) (or reuse EXCLUDED_TYPES) from server/utils/pokeapi.ts and use it here.

findings.issue: humanize is implemented twice (app/app/utils/format.ts:3 and app/server/utils/pokeapi.ts:51); a display-name fix applied to one silently misses the other.
findings.suggestion: Move humanize (and orDash/dexNumber, which the server would also want) into shared/utils/ — Nuxt auto-imports it into both the Vue app and server bundles (nuxt.com/docs/4.x/directory-structure/shared).

findings.issue: Each page hand-declares its response interface (PokemonData, MoveData, AbilityData, TypeData, IndexData) while the server routes return untyped object literals — no single source of truth at the boundary, and interface TypeRef is copy-pasted in three pages.
findings.suggestion: Declare the response shapes once in shared/types/, have the server routes annotate their returns with them, and import the same types in the pages.

findings.issue: No typescript/vue-tsc devDependencies and no typecheck script, yet the app writes ~95 lines of interfaces; Nuxt deliberately does not type-check on nuxt build, so the duplicated page/server types are never verified.
findings.suggestion: Add vue-tsc + typescript as devDependencies and a "typecheck": "nuxt typecheck" script (or typescript.typeCheck: true) per nuxt.com/docs/4.x/guide/concepts/typescript.

findings.issue: Upstream fetches have no timeout/abort, so a hung PokeAPI request stalls an SSR page indefinitely and pins a rejected-promise slot in the cache.
findings.suggestion: fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) }) and keep the existing catch(() => cache.delete(key)) eviction.

findings.issue: API base URL read from process.env at call time instead of Nuxt runtime config, which is the documented, deployment-portable way (Nitro presets, per-env overrides).
findings.suggestion: runtimeConfig: { apiBaseUrl: '' } in nuxt.config.ts (NUXT_API_BASE_URL / API_BASE_URL mapping) and read it via useRuntimeConfig().apiBaseUrl inside handlers.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled fetch wrapper with an explicit key and dedupe plus a `data as Ref<T>` cast; Nuxt 4.4 shipped createUseFetch factories for exactly this pattern.
findings.suggestion: Optionally rebuild usePageData on createUseFetch((opts) => ...) and let the framework merge defaults; at minimum drop the cast by type-checking the null/error union.

findings.issue: Query string handled by manual key.split('?') and template concatenation instead of the URL/URLSearchParams platform APIs.
findings.suggestion: Build the upstream URL with new URL(...) and url.searchParams, which also removes the hand-trimmed path normalization.

findings.issue: A bespoke TTL/promise-dedupe cache with an ad-hoc size cap duplicates what Nitro provides natively.
findings.suggestion: Not urgent — the implementation is correct and small; consider Nitro's defineCachedEventHandler / route rules if the caching policy ever grows.

findings.issue: nuxt is pinned to ^4.6.2 while 4.6.3 (2026-10-27) ships security fixes for the dev server and path handling advisories.

summary: This is a modern, current-generation Nuxt app: Nuxt 4.6 with the app/ directory layout, Vue 3.5 / vue-router 5, useId, useFetch behind a single composable, and zero dependencies beyond the framework itself. All upstream PokeAPI knowledge is isolated in one server module, so a framework upgrade would touch very little. The remaining churn risk is duplication the framework already solves — humanize and the excluded-type rule implemented twice, response shapes redeclared by hand in five pages, and no type-checking in the build to catch any of it drifting.
